title: Who, which, that, whose
goal: Join sentences with who, which, that and whose
intro: Relative pronouns let you describe someone or something inside one sentence: “The man who called you is my boss.” Use “who” for people, “which” for things, “that” for both, and “whose” to show belonging.

rules.rule: who for people, which for things, that for either.
examples: The girl who sings is my niece.
The phone that I bought is fast.
That’s the man whose car was stolen.
I have a friend whose father is a pilot.

rules.rule: Don’t repeat the pronoun after who/which.
examples: The book which I read was long. (not “which I read it”)
The lady who lives next door is kind.

mistakes.wrong: The person which called you is here.
mistakes.right: The person who called you is here.

mistakes.wrong: The film which I saw it was boring.
mistakes.right: The film which I saw was boring.

mistakes.wrong: I have a friend who his father is a pilot.
mistakes.right: I have a friend whose father is a pilot.

mistakes.wrong: This is the laptop who I use.
mistakes.right: This is the laptop that I use.

ex.q: The doctor ___ treated me was very kind.
This is the restaurant ___ serves the best dosa.
I met a woman ___ son studies with mine.
The bag ___ you gave me is really useful.
The teacher which taught us maths has retired.
ex.fixed: The teacher who taught us maths has retired.

ex.q: The house that we bought it is very old.
ex.fixed: The house that we bought is very old.

ex.q: He is the boy who his bike was stolen.
ex.fixed: He is the boy whose bike was stolen.

ex.q: Do you know anyone ___ can fix a washing machine?

ex.a: The man who lives upstairs is a chef.

ex.q: Join them with “who”: “I have a friend. She lives in London.”
a: I have a friend who lives in London

talk: Describe three people you know using who or whose: “I have a friend who…”, “My neighbour, whose son…”.
